That is TRUE but materially incomplete, and the missing half is load-bearing. ground-truth.md:46-53 verbatim: 'Lafayette, Louisville and Niwot are Xcel-electric and cannot access Efficiency Works at all, so no stacking statement of any kind applies to them. R4.programs_note: Bare 'Xcel' added 2026-09-17. DCI's llms.txt line 'Xcel rebate-stack eligibility' -- 1 occurrence, unchanged across every tree, survivor of five stacking sweeps and ten adversarial reads -- was still missed because 'Xcel' was not in this list. Safe to add because names_in() is SPAN-CONSUMING: one mention of 'Xcel Energy' yields ONE canonical name, not two.
R4.program_aliases_reason: Bare 'Xcel' and 'Xcel Energy' are ONE program. Without this map a single sentence reading 'According to Xcel Energy, its ... Xcel ...' resolved to TWO distinct program names and satisfied R4's two-distinct-programs test by itself. Span-consuming matching stops one MENTION counting twice; only an alias map stops two mentions of the same utility counting as two programs.  DESCRIPTIVE FORMS ADDED 2026-09-18 (GATE_SCORE_2026-09-17.md MISS 4): GCI's FAQPage stacking denial named its two programs as 'the free state weatherization program' and 'the Atmos rebate', while R4.programs held only the literals 'Colorado Weatherization Assistance Program' and 'Atmos Energy'. One program resolved, distinct<2, NEUTRAL, filtered. An alias is only added where its canonical program is already in THIS property's programs list.
